newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Salvadoran church recommends Romero for sainthood.
newsitem.headline: Salvadoran church recommends Romero for sainthood.

text.p: The Roman Catholic Church in El Salvador said on Friday it had asked the Vatican to consider slain Archbishop Oscar Arnulfo Romero for sainthood.
"We hope that, God willing, we'll be able to see Monsignor Romero in the altars by the year 2000," said Gregorio Rosa Rosa Chavez, the auxiliary bishop of San Salvador.

Romero, the archbishop of San Salvador and the so-called "voice of the voiceless," was a powerful advocate for the poor and a leading critic of the former military government in El Salvador when he was assassinated while saying mass on March 24, 1980.
His killers were never caught but a special government commission later linked his murder to right-wing death squads used to terrorise the opposition in the 1980s.

His martyrdom became a rallying cry for leftists and human rights activists during El Salvador's 12-year civil war, which ended in 1992, and his life was featured in the Hollywood movie "Romero" starring the late Raul Julia.
The Salvadoran church sent two boxes full of documents, books and testimonials on Romero's life to the Vatican on Friday.
